title: The Cup of Water
moral: Compassion means noticing someone’s need and helping at the right time, even if we miss something we wanted.

pages.text:
It was the hottest day of the month.

The school playground looked bright and dusty. Children ran slowly, as if the sun had made their shoes heavier.

During games period, Coach Ravi said, "Today we will practise relay running."

Amaan loved relay races. He liked holding the baton and running fast.

His team was winning in practice.

Just before the final round, Amaan saw the gardener sitting near the tap. He was wiping his forehead with a towel. Beside him were empty plant pots and a heavy sack of soil.

Amaan looked at the race track.

His team was calling him.

"Come fast!" shouted Rishi. "You are last runner!"

Amaan picked up the baton.

Then he saw the gardener try to stand, but sit back down again.

Amaan hesitated.

Rishi waved both hands. "Amaan! Race!"

Amaan ran, but not to the track.

He ran to the water cooler, filled a steel cup, and took it to the gardener.

"Uncle, please drink," he said.

The gardener looked surprised. "Thank you, beta."

Amaan quickly filled another cup and placed it beside him.

By then, the race had started without him. His team lost.

Rishi came over, breathing hard.

"We needed you!" he said.

Amaan looked down. "I know."

Rishi saw the gardener drinking water quietly. His face changed.

"Oh," he said.

Coach Ravi walked over.

"Amaan missed the race," Rishi said, "but he did something important."

The gardener smiled. "Very important."

Coach Ravi nodded. "A race can happen again. Kindness must be done when it is needed."

The next round, Coach Ravi made a new race. This time, every team had to carry a cup of water without spilling it.

Rishi spilled half on his own shoe.

"My shoe is refreshed," he said.

Everyone laughed.

The gardener clapped from the shade as Amaan finished. Amaan did not win the first race, but he felt like he had crossed a better finish line.
